text:
Scale: the plate looks like a dinner plate, but it is photographed at an angle. It spans roughly 560 px, so I took it as about 26 cm, or about 21.5 px per cm.

Roast chicken: this is a breast piece with skin, plus some loose skin and shreds. It covers about 400 x 250 px, which is roughly 18 x 11 cm, and it is about 5 cm thick at the breast. That gives a volume of about 300 cm³ at roughly 50% fill, so about 150 cm³, or about 150 g of meat. I added about 30 g for skin and loose pieces. The total is roughly 190 g with some bone possible, so I settled on 180 g.

Bread roll: it measures about 380 px long, or about 17 cm, and is about 5 cm wide and 4 cm tall. That is roughly 17 x 5 x 4 x 0.6, which is about 200 cm³. At a density of about 0.25 g/cm³ this comes to about 50 g. A small baguette roll would typically weigh 60 g, so I used 60 g.
